items.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: But then I was like who’s this? Miles Davis doing “My Funny Valentine”? But I didn’t know how he did it like that and she did it like that.

ctx.x: The part about, you said your brother used to take you on his bike to your first piano lessons and it got me thinking about piano lessons and how they relate and I wonder, can you recall when you first encountered chord symbols and then what do I do with these?

Without a doubt. You know my mother, jazz was a reward for practicing. Because I just wanted to go straight to jazz. And she was like no, you’re going to do this, you’re going to study classical, blah blah blah. And then you can play jazz. Which was kind of, when I look back on it, it really put the foundation in me for musical theory and different things like that. And then I played a little bit of organ at the church around the corner, at a Lutheran church, so this was a pipe organ when I was still a teenager.…
